title: Personal Credit Cards: when a points statement credit is made and its amount
content:
# Personal Credit Cards: threshold and amount of a points statement credit

This rule belongs to the Personal Credit Cards line. When a cardholder uses rewards points to pay down a card's balance, it decides whether the statement credit is made at all and fixes its USD amount.

## Rule

1. No statement credit is made when the card's balance is zero or below.
2. No statement credit is made when the points to be applied are fewer than the tier's smallest redemption.
3. Otherwise the statement credit uses the points to be applied, and its amount is those points multiplied by the tier's cash value per point, rounded half-up to the cent.

## Truth table

| Balance above zero | Points to be applied at least the smallest redemption | Statement credit |
|---|---|---|
| yes | yes | made, for the points to be applied |
| yes | no | not made |
| no | any | not made |

## Worked examples (hypothetical terms: smallest redemption 1000 points, cash value 0.03 USD per point)

| Balance | Points to be applied | Credit |
|---|---|---|
| 215.38 USD | 7180 | 7180 points, 215.40 USD |
| 215.38 USD | 900 | none, below the smallest redemption |
| 0.00 USD | any | none |

With a hypothetical value per point of 0.0175 USD, 1001 points give 17.5175 USD, rounded half-up to 17.52 USD.

## Wrong reading and correct basis

- **Wrong:** make a small credit for whatever points there are. **Correct:** below the smallest redemption no statement credit is made.
- **Wrong:** round the credit down to protect the balance. **Correct:** round half-up to the cent.
